reason: The sources comprehensively support a surprising, fast-paced story with well over 10 mutually-backed atomic claims.
story: Our solar system is currently drifting through the center of a gigantic, 1,000-light-year-wide cavity known as the Local Bubble. Filled with hot, million-degree plasma, this cosmic void was blasted out by a chain of roughly 15 ancient supernovae that began exploding about 14 million years ago. While the Sun was originally far away from the carnage, its galactic path carried it straight into the interior of the bubble around five million years ago. As the titanic stellar explosions blew gas and dust outward, they created a dense, frigid shell on the surface of the bubble. Today, every single young star and star-forming region within 500 light-years of Earth sits right on the edge of this expanding shell, acting as a massive stellar nursery. Researchers discovered this galactic history using data from the European Space Agency's Gaia observatory, proving that dying stars literally build the next generation of suns.
angle: Our solar system is currently floating right in the middle of a 1,000-light-year-wide cosmic void blasted out by 15 ancient star explosions.

claims.claim: The Local Bubble is approximately 1,000 light-years in size.
The Local Bubble is a cavity filled with low-density, high-temperature plasma.
About 15 supernovae are calculated to have gone off to form the Local Bubble.
The series of supernovae that created the Local Bubble began about 14 million years ago.
All nearby young stars and star-forming regions within 500 light-years of Earth sit on the surface of the Local Bubble.
The Sun entered the Local Bubble about 5 million years ago.
The European Space Agency's Gaia observatory provided crucial data used to map the bubble and stellar trajectories.
The Local Bubble is currently expanding at a speed of about 4 miles per second.
The Sun currently sits almost right in the center of the Local Bubble.
The gas within the Local Interstellar Cloud, where the Solar System resides, has a density of approximately 0.3 atoms per cubic centimeter.
Radioactive iron-60 isotopes found in deep-sea sediments and crusts have a peak linked to the solar system entering the Local Bubble.
Astronomers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian and the Space Telescope Science Institute published the 2022 Nature study on the bubble's history.

disputed: Exact source association for the supernovae: S1 mentions subgroups Lower Centaurus–Crux (LCC), Upper Centaurus–Lupus (UCL), or Pleiades moving group subgroup B1, while other sources broadly refer to a chain of 15 supernovae. Script should attribute specific subgroup claims or stick to the general 15 supernovae consensus.
